text:
Sam W.: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — ran into a couple of productiony edge cases for private endpoint cert renewal when control plane is separated from tenant VPC. Wanted to capture proposals and tradeoffs here.

Maria L.: TL;DR? I skimmed the RFC but didn't see the lifecycle for renewal during CP outage windows.

Sam W.: Short version: currently we assume control plane can sign CSRs on-demand. With separated/private control plane modes that may be unreachable from the tenant's renewal agent (firewalled), so renewals fail and endpoints go into degraded state. Need a pattern that works when control plane is logically separated and when customers prefer no inbound CP connectivity.

Jin K.: Hmm. Two modes we should support: 1) CP-initiated push (control plane opens signed cert into customer's S3-like artifact bucket / object store the agent can read) and 2) agent-initiated pull with offline signing. Both fail if the signing authority can't be accessed.

Nick P.: Concern: exposing signing keys or giving any customer-side signer KMS access is a no-go for security/compliance. Any delegated signer must be ephemeral and strictly scoped.

Maria L.: +1 on scoped ephemeral creds. Also worried about race conditions during cluster autoscaling where many agents try renewal at once. We should avoid N^2 CSR storms.

Sam W.: Agreed. Proposal A (stateless): short-lived control-plane-signed tokens minted at onboarding time with TTL ~24h. Agent holds token, uses it to fetch a signed cert artifact from CP object endpoint. If token expired, agent falls back to exponential retry and local self-signed cert until manual rotation. Pros: simple, no KMS exposure. Cons: token TTL vs security tradeoff and need to rotate tokens on host reprovision.

Sam W.: Proposal B (delegated CSR workflow): agent generates CSR locally, stores CSR in tenant VPC artifact (e.g., object store or SSM param), control plane pulls CSR out-of-band (pull initiated by CP when it has network path) signs it with CA, pushes signed cert back into artifact. Requires CP to periodically poll tenant artifacts or use a scheduled worker. Pros: CP retains CA keys, agent doesn't hold long-lived tokens. Cons: requires artifact glue and poller scheduling; adds latency.

Jin K.: Another variant: pre-signed CSR (like presigned upload). During onboarding CP mints a single-use presigned upload URL for CSRs, agent uploads CSR, CP signs and writes cert to a presigned download path. That reduces the need for persistent tokens. But presigned URLs still need lifecycle management and revocation is hard.

Nick P.: For all of these we must ensure auditability. Signed cert metadata needs to include which CP instance signed it and what policy was used. Also need to tie cert issuance to onboarding policy so we can revoke quickly.

Maria L.: Operationally, we need an eviction/backoff strategy if CP can't reach tenant artifacts for >X hours. UX: surface "using self-signed certs, reduced security posture" state in console and send automated alert.

Sam W.: To avoid CSR storms: add jittered backoff + token bucket at agent level; and CP-side we can implement batching for signing jobs. E.g., agents write CSR to path /renewals/<agent-id>/<csr-id>. CP worker scans every 30s, batches up to 200 CSRs and signs in parallel.

Jin K.: Quick pseudocode for agent flow (very rough):

```
# agent renewal loop
if has_unexpired_token():
  cert = http_get(cp_cert_artifact_url, auth=token)
  if cert valid: install(cert); continue
csr = gen_csr()
upload(csr_path)
# poll for signed cert with jittered exponential backoff
for attempt in range(0, N):
  cert = try_download(signed_cert_path)
  if cert: install(cert); break
  sleep(jittered_backoff())
# fallback local self-signed + alert
```

Nick P.: For KMS: CP should hold CA keys in HSM/KMS. Signing worker should run in CP control plane with strict IAM. No customer-side KMS usage. If we ever allow delegated in-vpc signing, it must be an HSM-backed ephemeral signing instance with attestation and limited lifetime. That adds heavy ops. Avoid unless customers explicitly request on-prem CA.

Maria L.: What about certificate revocation? We don't want stale certs lingering if CP revokes. We need a revocation list or short TTL certs (<24h) to reduce blast radius. Short TTL increases renewal churn. Tradeoff again.

Sam W.: My leaning: default flow = presigned CSR upload + CP signing worker (Proposal B variant with presigned uploads to avoid long-lived tokens). Default cert TTL = 24h. For high-security enterprise, offer option: dedicated in-VPC signer with attested short-lived HSM instance (opt-in).

Jin K.: Agree. Also add telemetry: counts of failed renewals, time-to-rotation, and percent of agents on self-signed fallback. These feed Optimize recommendations and alerting.

Nick P.: Implementation checklist: 1) artifact API for presigned upload/download; 2) signing worker with batching and HSM integration; 3) agent backoff + jitter library; 4) console UI for cert state + alerting; 5) audit logging schema.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: infra/artifacts-service -> staging at 2026-03-18T15:00Z (no downtime expected).

Sam W.: Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with the chosen default flow (presigned CSR + CP signing worker), include failure modes and operator runbooks. Can folks +1 or add major objections here?

Maria L.: +1. Add the revocation/TTL discussion as a separate appendix so we can iterate.

Jin K.: +1. I'll spike the signing worker prototype and share results in a follow-up thread.

Nick P.: +1, but add a hard requirement: all signing workers must log signing identity and be tied to the tenant ACL for audit.

Sam W.: Awesome — thanks all. I'll open the addendum this afternoon and tag you for review. :rocket:
